speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, I watch with concern the latest VDS measures.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I am particularly disturbed by this latest measure that puts the livelihoods of the unvaccinated at risk.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Former Singaporean tennis player, Jaime Wong, started a petition on this issue on 1 January 2022.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: She was a national tennis champion and represented Singapore in many international competitions, including SEA Games and the International Tennis Federation Fed Cup.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In her petition, she shared that, with effect from 15 January, she would no longer be able to continue her profession as a tennis coach nor enter the tennis school that she started because she is unvaccinated.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is heartening to note that amongst them are fully vaccinated Singaporeans acting out of concern for the livelihoods of the unvaccinated.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This means that we need to accept differences, not just differences in race, language, religion or culture but also differences in opinions and views.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We need to respect decisions that may be different from ours.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is not for fear of infecting others, because vaccination does not stop the transmission of COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The risk is, therefore, mainly to themselves, not others.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But I also believe that these 52,000 people are, at least, as concerned about their own health and safety as the Government is, if not more so.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: They must have strong reasons, based on their own individual circumstances and personal medical history, for sticking to their decision not to vaccinate, despite the VDS measures that had been progressively put in place, placing various restrictions on their movements and activities.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: To them, the risk, or cost, of vaccination must have been significant.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This latest measure that threatens their livelihood would just place them between a rock and a hard place.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There are many legitimate questions on the vaccines that are as yet unanswered.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What are the effects of repeated jabs administered every six months?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: When faced with a situation that is relatively new and where there are many gaps in our knowledge and information, it is always a good idea to keep an open mind, treat current knowledge with caution and not be too absolute in our measures because new knowledge could emerge later to prove us wrong.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A good example would be the Government's stand on masks in the initial stage of the pandemic.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Japan has a policy of no discrimination against the unvaccinated and they achieved a vaccination rate of 79% of their population versus our 87%.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, yes, our VDS probably pushed up our vaccination rate by a few percentage points, but there is the question of degree and the law of diminishing returns.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is often said that punishment must fit the crime.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The same principle should apply to non-criminal actions as well.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The consequences that we seek to impose should fit the action.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In making the choice between the risk of COVID-19 infection and the risk of adverse effects of vaccination and, where the risk falls primarily on themselves, is the loss of livelihood a befitting penalty?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This ban on the unvaccinated returning to their workplace and, thus, risking their livelihoods, is too harsh.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Even though the Government has asserted that every effort will be made to enable them to work from home, this is not always practical for every job affected.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The new measure is essentially “licence to terminate”.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And what is the expected benefit of imposing such a strong measure?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Even without this latest measure, on 5 December 2021, we achieved a vaccination rate of 96% of the eligible population then.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: With the threat of loss of livelihood, will we achieve 97%, 99%?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will the number of daily COVID-19 cases drop from 840 to 830?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Government policies are made based on macro considerations and statistics designed to benefit the majority.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Just as there are exceptions to every rule, there will always be a small group which would be adversely affected.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: While it is understandable that Government policies cannot possibly cater to every single individual, we can, at least, recognise the existence of exceptions and leave room for them.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Do not put them between a rock and a hard place.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What is the number of unvaccinated self-employed persons or gig workers?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What is the breakdown by age and industry?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: How many of them are expected to lose their jobs?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Has the Government studied the impact on these 52,000 unvaccinated employees and an unknown number of unvaccinated SEPs before making its decision?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: They are not mere statistics; they have elderly parents, they have children.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For those who lose their current jobs because they are unvaccinated, what is the likelihood of them finding another?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Measures that threatened livelihoods should never be taken lightly.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: They may become marginalised if they are unable to regain employment.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The prospect of an impending GST hike does not help matters.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Throughout the pandemic, the Government has taken great pains to keep our borders and our economy open, even at the risk of importing COVID-19 cases.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For the sake of economic gains, the Government has chosen to manage the health risk.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Please now extend the same consideration to the unvaccinated, recognise the importance to them of keeping their livelihood and allow them to manage their health risk.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What is the risk of overwhelming our healthcare system by allowing the 52,000 unvaccinated employees to return to their workplace?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Earlier today, the Minister for Health shared that the unvaccinated comprise two-thirds of the ICU cases.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is presumably based on a period of time when our vaccination rate was lower and the proportion of unvaccinated people in the population higher.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Based on MOH's statistics, our vaccination rate reached 50% on 18 July 2021.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Therefore, for the bigger part of 2021, more than half of our population was unvaccinated.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: While it is undeniable that the unvaccinated are more prone to serious cases, attributing the high number of unvaccinated cases of ICU or death in 2021 to the current small number of unvaccinated is misleading.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These are not ratios we can use to project into the future.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Focusing on the 52,000 unvaccinated employees, I do not have the information that will allow me to get a good estimate of the expected number that will fall seriously ill.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, the age breakdown of the unvaccinated is a key piece of information.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, as a ballpark figure would help form a clearer picture by indicating the order of magnitude, I have used whatever limited information I can find to arrive at a rough estimate.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Assuming the number of daily cases to be 800 out of a population of 5.5 million, applying that proportion to the 52,000 unvaccinated employees gives us 7.6 cases.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, assuming that most of them are below the age of 60, I used the ICU rate of 2.4%, which is the highest rate amongst those under 60.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Applying the rate of 2.4% on the 7.6 cases gives us 0.18 case requiring ICU per day.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If the number of cases were to double to 1,600 per day, that would give us 0.36 cases requiring ICU.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If the number of daily cases reaches 3,000, that would give us 0.68 ICU cases, bearing in mind that Omicron is expected to be more infectious but less severe, as shared by Minister for Health earlier today.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The vaccination of children aged five to 11 started in December last year, with only the mRNA option.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There are differing schools of thought on COVID-19 vaccinations and even more so for the vaccination of children, with several medical doctors publicly opposing it.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The unanswered question on the long-term effects of mRNA vaccines is even more relevant for children who have another 70 to 80 years ahead of them.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Making the decision on behalf of their children is more stressful than making decisions for themselves.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Heavy on their minds is whether VDS will be imposed on their children.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: At this point in time, is the Government able to give an indicative timeline for the assessment of inactivated virus vaccines, like Sinovac, for children and the required conditions for approval?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This information will be helpful for parents making their decisions on the vaccination of their children.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Member raised several points for clarification, including the removal of the concession to allow unvaccinated workers to return to the workplace with a negative Pre-Event Test (PET) result and also her queries relating to extension of VDS to children.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Earlier today, the Minister for Health had responded to questions from Members.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: He highlighted our threefold response in living with COVID-19: vaccination and boosters, bolstering our healthcare capacity and calibrating our SMMs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Each is important in our response to Omicron and in ensuring that, in the longer term, we can resume our normal lives as far as possible.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As a result, throughout the pandemic, we find that two-thirds of our ICU beds are occupied by individuals who are unvaccinated.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: They are also more likely to be administered therapeutics, which are not cheap.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: So, although a small proportion of our population, they take up a disproportionate amount of medical and hospital resources and contribute to a significant amount of workload of our hospital staff.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is actual resources being drained because of people who fall ill because of COVID-19.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: First, by putting restrictions on their social activities, we protect the unvaccinated by preventing them from being overly exposed to the virus.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Member earlier said, well, it is just for them, right?

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: But that is not true because the second point is that, if fewer unvaccinated people get infected, we preserve our hospital capacity whilst allowing the rest to carry on normal activities as much as possible.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To set the context, the emergence of the Delta variant in May 2021 required quick action to be taken to contain the numerous outbreaks of clusters in the community and to minimise the risk of our healthcare capacity being overwhelmed.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Multi-Ministry Task Force (MTF) thus decided to significantly tighten our SMMs, resulting in a move to Phase Two (Heightened Alert) in May 2021.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At the same time, we further ramped up our vaccination efforts, resulting in improved vaccination rates, particularly among seniors.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Members will remember that our vaccination programme kicked off one year ago in early January 2021.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: By 9 August 2021, 72% of our entire population had completed their full regimen or received two doses of COVID-19 vaccines, with 81% receiving at least one dose.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: With this high level of vaccination coverage and through our collective efforts as a nation to comply with the strict Phase Two (Heightened Alert) measures, the daily number of COVID-19 cases fell to double digits.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The MTF thus restarted the process of resuming more economic and social activities through a calibrated risk-based approach aimed to protect the unvaccinated whilst not placing further strains on our healthcare system.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We thus introduced VDS for selected premises, activities and events from 10 August 2021.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through VDS, we eased measures for those who are fully vaccinated rather than hold everyone back in order to reduce the risk to the unvaccinated.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Fully vaccinated persons have good protection against the virus and are at lower risk of becoming dangerously ill if infected with COVID-19.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This would mean that they would not strain our resources.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: So, vaccination is still a very important and powerful measure in the many things that we are doing to protect our community from COVID-19.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We resumed dining in F&B establishments for groups of up to five vaccinated persons, with exemptions for children aged 12 and below.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We also allowed significant increases in event sizes, such as congregational and worship services, live performances and MICE, up to 500 persons, as long as all attendees were fully vaccinated.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Unvaccinated individuals, on the other hand, need to be more prudent in interacting with larger groups of people, especially in mask-off settings, which are high-risk.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Hence, the strict measures will continue to apply to them.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It will not matter if they are tennis coaches; the virus does not discriminate because it will impact you more severely if you are unvaccinated.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: With access to premises, activities and events being brought under the VDS framework, the hope was that this would also encourage the unvaccinated to get their vaccination so that they can participate in the community and society safely.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Despite our cautious approach to reopening, the heightened transmissibility of the Delta variant resulted in new clusters emerging by end August 2021.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This put great pressure on our healthcare system.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Sixty-six percent of ICU patients were unvaccinated or partially vaccinated individuals.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: They took up scarce medical resources, which are needed for others who are very sick individuals, including those with non-COVID-19 conditions who require expensive therapeutics.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To stabilise the situation, we had to roll out revised healthcare protocols and tighten our SMMs again.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: But we were able to allow more activities to continue during this Stabilisation Phase, compared to the earlier Phase Two (Heightened Alert) period due to VDS.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: VDS has also allowed us to safely resume more activities even after we exited the Stabilisation Phase on 22 November 2021.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: With more social interactions taking place over the year-end holidays, case numbers did not see a surge.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: But we need to decide whether we want to tighten up all our SMMs again, which would affect the lives and livelihoods of both the vaccinated and unvaccinated, or do we calibrate our measures so that we only tighten up for those who are unvaccinated and who would be more likely to impose strains on our healthcare system.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We need to calibrate; we need to balance.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through VDS, we hope to keep the unvaccinated individuals protected from infection whilst allowing the rest of society to continue with their normal activities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In line with our overall reopening approach, the MTF announced the introduction of the Workforce Vaccination Measures (WVM), which required that, from 1 January 2022, unvaccinated individuals who were medically eligible for vaccination would be required to produce a negative PET result before entering the workplace so as to mitigate the risks of workplace transmission.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The MTF subsequently announced on 14 December 2021 that up to 50% of those who can work from home will be allowed to return to the office from 1 January 2022 as we would be in a better position to ease the current default work-from-home posture with the WVM in place.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, we have seen the emergence of a more transmissible Omicron variant, which, with the Delta variant, significantly raises the risk of contracting COVID-19, compared to a year ago.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is a reduction from the 52,000 reported on 19 December 2021, as we have seen more employees coming forward to get vaccinated.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Among the unvaccinated employees, those aged 30 to 39 form the largest group at 16,000.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Whilst a negative PET is an indicator that the person is not infected with COVID-19, the unvaccinated individual has no protection against the virus.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: And if you think about it, if all the 48,000 get COVID-19, it would, indeed, impact on our healthcare system.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This decision was taken in consideration of many different factors and in consultation with many different stakeholders.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This move was supported by the tripartite partners who recognised the public health imperative of vaccination and the urgency to sustain business activity to protect livelihoods.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A fully vaccinated workforce would be able to operate more safely and sustainably.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We still allow employees who are certified medically ineligible for vaccines under the National Vaccination Programme (NVP) to return to the workplace, given that they constitute only 0.3% – a very small proportion – of unvaccinated workers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, whilst such employees are exempted from WVM, MOM and the tripartite partners have guided employers to give special consideration, such as allowing them to work from home, if they are able to do so, and redeploying them to suitable jobs which can be done from home, if such jobs are available.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: From the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, we had adopted a special approach to fully cover the costs of COVID-19 medical treatment for Singapore Citizens, Permanent Residents and Long-Term Pass Holders (SC/PR/LTPHs) who had not recently travelled.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This special approach was intended to avoid financial considerations adding to the public uncertainty and concern when COVID-19 was an emergent and unfamiliar disease.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Today, the vaccines have since become widely administered and there is sufficient evidence that they confer protection to reduce the risk of serious illness and death.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Those aged above 12 who remain unvaccinated by choice have decided to do so despite knowing that this places them at a higher risk of requiring costly inpatient care, which adds to the strain on our healthcare system.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The special treatment of the Government fully covering the costs of COVID-19 medical treatment will, therefore, not apply to this group.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This will also be the case for individuals aged above 18 who do not come forward for their booster within 270 days or nine months from their last dose.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Depending on the severity of the patient's condition and the type of COVID-19 facility where care is rendered, the bill size would vary, but these patients who are unvaccinated by choice may still tap on the regular healthcare financing arrangement to help pay for their bills, where applicable.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: SCs and PRs may also use their MediSave balance to help fund any remaining post-subsidy amount, subject to the claim limits that apply.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will, periodically, review our policies as the extension of the national COVID-19 vaccination programme to children aged five to 11 progresses.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Earlier today, we had also addressed concerns that were raised by Members.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: And we acknowledge that these are some legitimate concerns that parents may have.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: But given all the facts we have and in the current situation that we are facing, it is still highly encouraged for parents to bring their children if they are eligible for the vaccination.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Singapore is now in a better position to achieve our goal of being a COVID-19 resilient nation.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: The data in 2021 is based on a case where, for the first half of 2021, more than 50% of the population was unvaccinated.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: Can the Parliamentary Secretary provide us with the statistics for this?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But I do have some points to respond to the Member's queries.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Two, in terms of studying the implication on them, I appreciate that there will be concerns.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But we are also talking about the whole of nation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are talking about economic stability, the normal way of life that everyone else craves for.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We need to consider also how the economy will be impacted by just this small number taxing on our healthcare system and, because of these numbers, we then have to adjust and calibrate our SMMs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For those who are able to go out and are better protected, they then are able to have access to different things.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But for those who are then at-risk of getting COVID-19 and having severe illnesses, I think there have to be implications on the consequences that we have to accept and appreciate and, therefore, make a decision, calibrating all these needs and not talking about just one group, and a small group at that.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: I think it is quite hypothetical using the 1% on the 48,000 —

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Ms Hazel Poa, I am afraid the 30 minutes allocated for the Adjournment Motion has lapsed.
